title: Streamed JSON segment rescue and toolcall reconciliation
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Incoming streamed structured JSON can be cut at arbitrary token boundaries by truncation, network pauses, or client disconnects. When JSON fragments include escaped characters (" \n \t) or nested arrays/objects and interleaved tool/function call markers, naive line-delimited or bracket-repair heuristics can produce incorrect reassembly or duplicate tool invocations. This ticket defines a rescue and replay/resume design to reliably reconstruct partial JSON segments, reconcile toolcall boundaries, and provide a backward-compatible compatibility layer for older clients.

Problem specifics:
- Streams may be truncated mid-escape sequence (e.g., partial "\u\uXXXX") which breaks simple checksum or bracket counting heuristics.
- Tool/function calls can begin in one fragment and complete in another; replaying a full toolcall must be idempotent to avoid duplicate external side effects.
- Existing resume tokens only capture byte offsets and are insufficient when the generator state includes escape state and open-string context.
- Older clients expect newline-delimited JSON objects; new protocol messages would be optional and must degrade gracefully.

Goals:
1) Provide a deterministic, low-latency recovery path for partially-received structured outputs.
2) Avoid double-execution of tool calls (ensure idempotency or deduplication).
3) Add minimal API / wire-protocol extensions that are backward compatible.
4) Provide comprehensive tests and observability (metrics and traces) to detect segment corruption and replay frequency.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can detect and tag partially-complete JSON fragments with a deterministic fragment-state token
Clients can request resume using a resume_token that encodes parser state (open_braces_count, open_array_count, in_string_flag, escape_state_checksum) as a compact base64 string

Tool calls reconstructed after resume will include an idempotency_token; downstream integrations must be deduplicated using idempotency_token or the runtime will suppress duplicate invocation when it can verify semantic replay
Older clients continue to receive newline-delimited NDJSON fallback when new resume_token is not negotiated
implementation_notes: Introduce 'stream.checkpoint' event every N KB or on logical toolcall boundaries carrying a resume_token string
Resume token is a compact base64 blob: version|cursor|open_counts|in_string_flag|esc_hash where esc_hash is a 32-bit rolling hash of last 64 bytes to detect partial escape sequences
Escape-state machine added to runtime parser to track whether last chunk ends mid-backslash or mid-unicode-escape; escape state becomes part of resume_token

Toolcall wrapper: when runtime emits a tool call event it must include an idempotency_token and a deterministic fragment_signature; on resume if fragment_signature matches previously-executed record, runtime suppresses execution and re-emits outcome event

Compatibility: negotiate via stream header 'resume-v1' boolean; if absent, continue NDJSON-coercion path where runtime emits complete objects only after closing braces are balanced (may buffer longer)
qa_plan: Unit tests: parser state machine with artificially truncated byte sequences including mid-\\u escapes and surrogate pairs

Integration tests: end-to-end streaming session where connection is cut at 20 different offsets across nested objects and arrays; assert reassembled JSON equals reference and toolcall executed exactly once
Chaos tests: randomized truncation and reorder of chunks across multiple clients; assert resume_token prevents corruption
Compatibility tests: downgrade client negotiation and assert NDJSON fallback is produced and validated by older SDKs
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): runtime-1.19 on dedicated pool with resume-v1 enabled for 10% of streaming sessions; verbose logging of resume_token creation and replay metrics
Phase 2: expand to 50% with runtime dedup suppression active for verified integrations (GitHub PR, webhooks), collect false-positive/false-negative counts
Phase 3: full rollout with SDKs (node/python) exposing resume_token parsing helpers and example patterns for idempotent tool implementation
